seo.og_title: 2022 Toyota Crown import from Japan NZ
seo.og_description: Looking at a 2022 Toyota Crown for New Zealand? We help confirm whether it is the S220 sedan or S235 Crown Crossover, explain the hybrid options, and check current auction availability from Japan.

blocks.hero_subtitle: The 2022 Crown sits at the handover from the S220 sedan to the S235 Crown Crossover. Before bidding, we confirm the model code, grade and hybrid system so you know which Crown you are looking at.
proof_points: Importing estimate, with compliance as part of the process
blocks.why_kiwis_buy: People look at the Crown when they want a late-model Toyota with a quieter, more upmarket feel than a mainstream sedan. The useful detail with 2022 cars is knowing that the new Crown Crossover brought standard AWD hybrid drivetrains across the launch range, not just a badge change.
blocks.video_caption: If you are watching a 2022 Crown video, the key thing to spot is the body shape. A low S220 sedan and the taller S235 Crown Crossover sit under the same model name in 2022, and that changes the grade ladder and hybrid system.
blocks.main_usp_deep: The main appeal of the 2022 Crown is that you can target either the final traditional Crown sedan shape or the new Crown Crossover, depending on what you want from the car. On the Crown Crossover, Toyota split the range cleanly: X and G-series grades use the 2.5-litre A25A-FXS hybrid with E-Four, while RS grades get the 2.4-litre T24A-FTS turbo hybrid, Direct Shift-6AT and E-Four Advanced. That matters because an RS is not just a trim upgrade, it is a different drivetrain package. We confirm that from the auction list before any bid goes in.

buyer_persona.headline: Who is this car right for?
buyer_persona.body: This suits someone who wants a late-model Toyota with more presence and a more interesting drivetrain than the usual hybrid sedan. It also works for buyers who are happy to be specific about body style and grade, because with a 2022 Crown that detail matters from the start. If you want us to narrow it down to sedan or crossover first, this is a solid match.

car_specs_benefits.spec: S220 sedan built to June 2022, S235 Crown Crossover launched in July 2022 and on sale from autumn 2022
car_specs_benefits.benefit: That split is the first thing to get right, because a 2022 Crown can mean two different cars.
This is the mainstream Crown Crossover setup, aimed at smooth daily use with all-wheel-drive traction built into the hybrid package.

car_specs_benefits.spec: 2.4-litre T24A-FTS turbo hybrid with Direct Shift-6AT and E-Four Advanced AWD
car_specs_benefits.benefit: RS grades use a different drivetrain package, with a more stepped automatic feel under acceleration.

car_specs_benefits.spec: Launch grades: X, G, G Leather Package, G Advanced, G Advanced Leather Package, RS, RS Advanced
car_specs_benefits.benefit: The grade name tells you a lot about the car before you even get to options, especially whether it sits in the 2.5 hybrid range or the RS turbo-hybrid range.

car_specs_benefits.spec: A25A-FXS grades use a hybrid transaxle with reduction gear
car_specs_benefits.benefit: That setup supports the smoother low-speed response many buyers expect from a Toyota hybrid.

car_specs_benefits.spec: RS Advanced was the highest verified launch grade
car_specs_benefits.benefit: If you want the top launch specification, that is the grade to ask us to search for first.

standout_features_block.headline: What sets it apart
standout_features_block.intro: On a Crown, the worthwhile differences are the ones that change how easy the car is to shortlist and live with.

items.title: Two body styles under one 2022 model year
items.body: A 2022 Crown can be either the final S220 sedan or the newer S235 Crown Crossover. Getting that right early saves time and keeps your search focused on the shape and driving position you actually want.
items.image_hint: Side profile photo that clearly shows either the lower sedan shape or the taller crossover profile

items.title: Grade ladder with clear comfort-focused options
items.body: G, G Leather Package, G Advanced and G Advanced Leather Package give buyers several upper-trim paths before stepping into RS territory. That is useful if you want a more comfort-led Crown rather than choosing the range for its sportier badge.
items.image_hint: Front seats and cabin trim photographed from the open driver's door, showing upholstery and dashboard finish

items.title: Upper trims that are easy to target
items.body: The launch range gives you clear trim targets rather than one catch-all flagship. G Advanced Leather Package and RS Advanced are worth shortlisting first if you want a higher-spec car and want the search narrowed quickly.
items.image_hint: Interior dashboard and front cabin view with screens, steering wheel and front seats visible together

items.title: Crossover option for easier access
items.body: The S235 Crown Crossover adds a taller body style to the Crown name. For NZ buyers, that can mean easier entry and exit, a slightly higher seating position and a different feel from the traditional sedan.
items.image_hint: Three-quarter exterior photo showing the taller ride height and overall crossover profile

tech_deep_dive_block.headline: Under the skin
tech_deep_dive_block.intro: The 2022 Crown only makes sense once the drivetrain split is clear.

items.title: A25A-FXS hybrid with E-Four
items.body: This is the launch powertrain for X and the G-series Crown Crossover grades. It uses Toyota's hybrid transaxle with reduction gear rather than a conventional stepped automatic. E-Four adds an electrically driven rear axle. In daily driving that gives the car the smooth low-speed response people expect from a Toyota hybrid, with extra traction when the rear axle is called on.

items.title: T24A-FTS turbo hybrid with Direct Shift-6AT
items.body: RS and RS Advanced use a different idea altogether. The T24A-FTS turbo hybrid pairs a 2.4-litre turbo petrol engine with a Direct Shift-6AT, so it has a more stepped, conventional feel under load than the 2.5 hybrid setup. That is the practical difference many buyers miss when they assume every Crown hybrid drives the same.

items.title: E-Four versus E-Four Advanced
items.body: Toyota split the AWD systems as well as the engines. The 2.5 hybrid grades use E-Four, while the RS grades use E-Four Advanced. The key buying point is that Toyota tied each AWD system to a specific powertrain and grade family, so we confirm the exact grade and drivetrain on each car rather than relying on a broad Crown description.

blocks.how_to_use_iyc: Send us the model, year, body style you want, your budget and any must-have grade. We check current auction availability, explain what the auction list shows, and work out an importing estimate before you decide whether to bid.

faq_block.q: Why is the 2022 Toyota Crown harder to pin down than other model years?
faq_block.a: Because 2022 overlaps two different Crown directions. The S220 sedan ran to June 2022, then the S235 Crown Crossover launched later that year, so the model code matters from the start.

faq_block.q: What costs make up the importing estimate?
faq_block.a: We break it into Vehicle cost, Japan-side costs, Shipping costs, Customs clearance, Compliance and On-road costs. The exact total depends on the car you choose and the auction result.

faq_block.q: Can you tell me if a Crown is typically within the entry requirements before I bid?
faq_block.a: Import viability must be checked for the exact model code and vehicle before bidding. Final certification happens in New Zealand after arrival and assessment.

faq_block.q: How long does the process take?
faq_block.a: Timing depends on when a suitable car appears, whether your bid is successful, and the shipping schedule after purchase. We keep you updated through the process rather than guessing a fixed date upfront.

faq_block.q: What do you provide from the auction side?
faq_block.a: We translate and explain the auction list information available for the car, including grade, mileage, recorded notes, damage markings and listed modifications where shown. Photos and supporting records vary between listings.

city_use_case.headline: How NZ buyers usually narrow down a 2022 Crown
city_use_case.body: The first useful step is choosing the body style before comparing grades. The notes we see from around New Zealand are consistent: buyers in Auckland often start with current auction options and budget, Christchurch buyers often need the S220 sedan and S235 Crown Crossover split clarified first, Wellington buyers tend to focus on trim and drivetrain, Hamilton buyers benefit from listing-by-listing verification, and Tauranga buyers often shortlist by year, body style and preferred grade.

not_for_you_block.headline: Who this may not suit
items: If you want a simple one-version model search, the 2022 Crown can be frustrating because body style, grade and drivetrain need careful confirmation.
If you only want the classic low sedan shape, rule out the Crown Crossover early and search specifically for the S220 sedan.
If you want the newer Crown look but do not care about the RS drivetrain, a G-series Crown Crossover can make more sense than paying extra for the turbo-hybrid badge.

battery_health_block.body: For a Crown hybrid, the exact battery condition cannot be assumed from the model alone. If a listing includes battery-related notes, we explain what is written on the auction list and what is not confirmed there.
